questions.question: What is React's reconciliation (Fiber) algorithm?
questions.title: React Reconciliation (Fiber) — How React Updates the DOM
questions.direct_answer:
What is React's reconciliation (Fiber) algorithm?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Fiber architecture (rebranded from stack), work units, incremental rendering, priority lanes (React 18), diffing by type + key.

**Classic weak answer:** Saying React always re-renders the whole tree — it only re-renders matched subtrees and commits minimal DOM changes.

**Senior finish:** Mention React 18's concurrent rendering, priority lanes, and time-slicing; link to useTransition.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **React Reconciliation (Fiber) — How React Updates the DOM** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What is React's reconciliation (Fiber) algorithm?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Fiber architecture (rebranded from stack), work units, incremental rendering, priority lanes (React 18), diffing by type + key**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Saying React always re-renders the whole tree — it only re-renders matched subtrees and commits minimal DOM changes**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Mention React 18's concurrent rendering, priority lanes, and time-slicing; link to useTransition**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Fiber architecture (rebranded from stack), work units, incremental rendering, priority lanes (React 18), diffing by type + key
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

```mermaid
    COMMIT --> EF[useEffect after paint]

    end
    DIFF --> MEMO
```

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **saying React always re-renders the whole tree — it only re-renders matched subtrees and commits minimal DOM changes** and what you do instead.

- **Differentiator:** Mention React 18's concurrent rendering, priority lanes, and time-slicing; link to useTransition

sections.title: How to answer verbally (timed)
sections.content:
**Open (15–20 seconds):** Restate the question and give the one-sentence definition.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **Fiber architecture (rebranded from stack), work units, incremental rendering, priority lanes (React 18), diffing by type + key** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Saying React always re-renders the whole tree — it only re-renders matched subtrees and commits minimal DOM changes** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

**Finish (15–20 seconds):** Add **Mention React 18's concurrent rendering, priority lanes, and time-slicing; link to useTransition**, then offer a trade-off question back (“do you optimize for TTFB or TTI here?”).

questions.question: Why do React keys matter? What are the pitfalls of using array index as a key?
questions.title: React Keys Explained — Why Index as Key Is a Bug
questions.direct_answer:
Why do React keys matter? What are the pitfalls of using array index as a key?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Keys identify items across renders; stable keys preserve component state; index changes when list reorders, causing wrong state mapping.

**Classic weak answer:** Using the array index as a key for a sortable/filterable list — state attaches to position, not item.

**Senior finish:** Show a classic bug: reversing a list with index keys causes input values to stick to positions instead of items.
